author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Just reading the markets this morning, and holy shit...

S&P futures were down 1.4% overnight after the Democrats swept Congress. Nasdaq futures were down 2.4%.

Now the S&P is UP over 1% and Dow futures are up 800+ points. That's a 2.5% swing in a matter of hours.

Two days ago I said the Democrats would win the House (and likely the Senate). They won both. The knee-jerk reaction was to dump AI stocks on fears a Democratic Congress goes after the data center boom.

Then Trump accepted the results, reminded everyone he still has the veto, and the selling stopped.

Gridlock. Markets love gridlock. The S&P has finished higher one year after every single midterm since 1982.

But here's what nobody is talking about this morning... Iran.

Iran's strategy worked.

Not completely, but it worked.

They hit the oil market. Brent went from around $70 before the war to over $100, gas prices surged, and voters felt it every time they filled up.

Even Trump admitted last night "a part of it was Iran." You'd be a fool to say it was the only factor... but it mattered.

So now we know Iran's playbook for the next round of attacks, and nobody even knows who's actually running shit over there. The next round could be close too...

We have the biggest US military buildup in the region since 2003, with reports the US and Israel have strikes planned if talks fall apart.

The big difference now is Trump doesn't have to worry about another election. Inflation be damned. Higher gas prices won't cost him a thing at the ballot box anymore.

A Democratic Congress will try to handcuff him. They can pass a war powers resolution, but Trump vetoes it, and they need two-thirds of both chambers to override. Good luck with that.

So stocks are partying over gridlock this morning while oil is still pricing a war that could be about to get a whole lot worse.

Lots of variables right now. Keep a close eye on energy.

Be careful out there.
